answers.notes: I sing and play at gigs. I want cleaner fast runs and richer chords under my voice.

note: A demo week for an advanced singer who plays guitar: three practice days of about 45 minutes, taken from the first week of a compare-models Fable 5.2 run of 2026-11-15, with the vowel guide added. Runs are the key skill and return on all three days: a five-note run faster in stages, a run aimed at the chord that is arriving, pentatonic runs at speed and runs over a soul vamp. On guitar, 9th chords, the 3rd and 7th of each chord, sus and add9 chords and a two-chord vamp sit under the voice, and each day ends with singing over the backing track.

plan.title: Week 1: fast runs, rich chords
plan.summary: Three practice days of about 45 minutes, voice and guitar in turn. Day 1 takes a five-note run faster in stages, plays Am9, D9 and Gmaj7 and sings guide tones over the same ii–V–I in G. Day 2 takes five vowels across the break, finds the 3rd and 7th of each chord on guitar, sings the hard leaps and aims a run at the next chord. Day 3 is pentatonic runs at speed and a soul vamp: you comp it on guitar, then sing runs over it.
plan.progress:
Runs: a five-note run faster in stages, pentatonic runs at speed, runs aimed at the 3rd of the next chord, runs over a soul vamp. Next: turns, then the octave run.
Extended chords: Am9, D9 and Gmaj7; the 3rd and 7th of each chord; sus and add9 on top; a two-chord soul vamp comped. Next: Dm9, G9 and Cmaj7, then a turnaround over the backing track.
Intervals & leaps: the 7ths, the tritone and the minor 6th, each found from a neighbour note. Next: tunes with wide leaps.
Harmony & improvising: guide tones over the ii–V–I in G. Next: a line of their own over the ii–V–I in C.
Breath & range: short warm-ups (breath and a lip roll; the middle, then light and high) and five vowels across the break. Keep as warm-up.
Building chords: names minor 7, dominant 7 and major 7 chords by ear. Next: the same, faster.
Ear: names intervals by ear. Next: read the ratings before building on it.
